name: Zendesk
subcategory: help desks, live chat and support knowledge
tagline: Operate a small email and web support inbox with tickets and an audit trail

pricing.notes: Official Suite Team monthly agent price.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Zendesk, operate a small email and web support inbox with tickets and an audit trail. The hard boundary is omnichannel routing, marketplace, workforce tools, reporting, compliance, and support, plus channel integrations and support operations.
coreLoopDIY: Receive customer email and web messages, route them into a shared ticket inbox, reply from one place, and retain a searchable conversation history with an audit trail.
whatYouLose: omnichannel routing, marketplace, workforce tools, reporting, compliance, and support
ongoingBurden: message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Zendesk because support software survives because missing or misrouting one customer message is expensive and every channel behaves differently. The recurring cost buys message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Chatwoot
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source customer engagement and shared-inbox platform.

alternatives.name: Chatwoot
alternatives.desc: A proper support inbox with chat, email and a help center; free software, billable server chores.

alternatives.name: Frappe Helpdesk
alternatives.desc: Tickets, SLAs and a knowledge base in a clean Frappe shell; the five-minute installer still leaves you the pager.

alternatives.name: FreeScout
alternatives.desc: Email becomes an assigned team inbox with notes and collision warnings; the nicer modules open a wallet.

alternatives.name: osTicket
alternatives.desc: Email and web forms become assigned tickets; dated, dependable and very much your PHP server.

alternatives.name: Zammad
alternatives.desc: A serious ticket desk with email, chat, SLAs and a knowledge base; setup is the first ticket.

alternatives.name: Odoo Helpdesk One App Free
alternatives.desc: A real hosted ticket desk for unlimited users, as long as Helpdesk is your one free Odoo app.

alternatives.name: tawk.to
alternatives.desc: Live chat, tickets, email, and a help centre for zero dollars; the tiny tawk.to badge pays the rent.

alternatives.name: LibreDesk
alternatives.desc: A modern email-and-live-chat desk in one compact stack, because apparently that was allowed.

rejectedAlternatives.name: FreeScout
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Email tickets are free; the customer portal and web form are a paid module.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Freshdesk Free Program
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free program expires after six months, so it cannot replace an ongoing desk.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Suite Team plan and a small-team shared inbox DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Zendesk in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: receive customer email and web messages, route them into a shared ticket inbox, reply from one place, and retain a searchable conversation history with an audit trail.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one workspace, agents, contacts, inboxes, conversations, messages, labels, and assignment.
Provide a website chat widget with reconnect, unread counts, file limits, and clear availability state.
Create a shared inbox with filters, collision warnings, notes, canned replies, and searchable history.
Add email notifications, browser notifications, and an immutable assignment and status log.
Implement spam controls, attachment scanning hooks, retention settings, export, and contact deletion.
Ship Docker Compose, backups, health checks, migrations, and a documented admin recovery flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out many social and messaging channels.
Deliberately leave out AI agents trained on proprietary support data.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workforce management, SSO, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
